subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A tRNA anticodon is 5'-UAC-3'. The mRNA codon it pairs with is:
questions.explain: Antiparallel complementary base pairing of anticodon 5'-UAC-3' gives codon 5'-GUA-3'.

questions.q: In epistasis, the phenotypic effect of one gene is:
options: Masked or modified by a different gene at another locus
questions.explain: Epistasis occurs when one gene at one locus masks or modifies the expression of a gene at a different locus.

questions.q: A totipotent stem cell differs from a pluripotent stem cell because it can:
options: Differentiate into any cell type including extra-embryonic (placental) tissue
questions.explain: Totipotent cells can form all cell types of the organism plus extra-embryonic tissues, unlike pluripotent cells.

questions.q: DNA polymerase can only add nucleotides to the 3' end of a strand. This explains why:
options: The leading strand is synthesised in fragments
The lagging strand is synthesised discontinuously as Okazaki fragments
Helicase is required to join the fragments
questions.explain: Because synthesis must run 5' to 3', the antiparallel lagging strand is built discontinuously as Okazaki fragments later joined by ligase.

questions.q: For a chi-squared test on a dihybrid cross with four phenotypic classes, the number of degrees of freedom is:
questions.explain: Degrees of freedom equal the number of categories minus one, so 4 - 1 = 3.

questions.q: Natural selection leads to evolution because:
options: Alleles that increase survival and reproduction become more frequent over generations
Individuals change their genes during their lifetime to suit the environment
questions.explain: Differential survival and reproduction of advantageous alleles increases their frequency in the gene pool over time.

questions.q: The ABO blood group system is an example of multiple alleles because:
options: There are more than two alleles in the population for one gene
Each person has more than two alleles
questions.explain: Three alleles (IA, IB, i) exist in the population for the single ABO gene, though each individual carries only two.

questions.q: Which of the following is a prezygotic reproductive isolating mechanism?
options: Differences in courtship behaviour preventing mating
questions.explain: Behavioural (courtship) isolation prevents mating, acting before a zygote can form, so it is prezygotic.

questions.q: Which type of mutation is most likely to alter every amino acid downstream of the mutation site?
options: A substitution at the third base of a codon
A deletion of a single base
questions.explain: A single-base deletion shifts the reading frame, changing all subsequent codons (a frameshift).

options: The population mean shifting towards one extreme phenotype
Both extremes being favoured over the mean
questions.explain: Directional selection favours one extreme, shifting the population mean in that direction over time.

questions.q: What is the role of DNA helicase during replication?
options: Proofreading newly added bases for errors
Joining adjacent nucleotides with phosphodiester bonds
Breaking the hydrogen bonds between complementary bases to unwind the double helix
Adding free nucleotides in a 3' to 5' direction
questions.explain: Helicase breaks the hydrogen bonds between base pairs, separating the two strands of the double helix.

questions.q: In PCR, the temperature is raised to around 95 degrees C in order to:
options: Separate the two DNA strands by breaking hydrogen bonds
questions.explain: Denaturation at ~95 degrees C breaks the hydrogen bonds, separating the DNA into single strands.
